title: Tenant query shaping and chunked prefetch protocol for low tail latency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a query shaping layer and a chunked prefetch protocol for the Console dashboard query API to reduce tail latency for tenants with bursty, deep-scroll patterns while controlling cost via per-tenant TTLs and budget-aware hedging.
background: Current dashboard pagination approaches use fixed page sizes and a single shared prefix cache with global TTLs. We observe long tail latency when customers issue deep scrolls or run complex cohort queries; these patterns cause expensive fanout queries and hot-key eviction churn. Existing measures (read hedging + speculative prefetch) help but are either too aggressive (cost blowup) or too conservative (no tail reduction).
solution_overview: Introduce a thin query-shaping service in front of the dashboard query API that rewrites pagination requests into 'chunked windows' (N-token/row chunks) and drives a chunked prefetch protocol: when serving a chunk, we asynchronously prime the next chunk(s) based on a probabilistic next-page predictor that uses tenant history + route heuristics. Complement with dynamic TTL and soft-eviction hints per chunk keyed by (tenant, route, anchor-window) so hot deep-scroll prefixes are kept longer while cold prefixes expire quickly. Add cost-aware throttles that cap prefetch concurrency per-tenant and fall back to a lightweight summary response if budget thresholds are exceeded.
technical_design_notes: Query shaping responsibilities: translate client pagination params (cursor/offset/page_size) to chunk windows and add metadata header X-Chunk-Anchor.
Chunk format: stable chunk id derived from tenant id + route + anchor + sequence number; include small content hash to detect staleness.

Prefetch predictor: lightweight logistic model served in runtime (features: tenant recent scroll depth, route type, time-of-day, previous contiguous reads). Default fallthrough uses simple heuristic: >1 contiguous reads in last minute -> prefetch next 2 chunks.
Cache store changes: namespace cache by chunk id and store soft-eviction_hint attribute which adjusts LRU weight; TTL policy is per-tenant continuous score mapped from usage and cost budget.

Hedging & backpressure: prefetches are non-blocking, but if origin latency exceeds threshold or memstore pressure is high, we stop prefetch for that tenant and immediately serve a reduced summary response with 'more_available' flag.
Instrumentation: emit metrics per-chunk (prefetch_count, prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_cost_tokens, tail_latency_95/99 by tenant), and a budget_consumed gauge.
Compatibility: API surface remains backward-compatible; clients see identical cursor semantics. We only change server-side cursor encoding to include chunk offsets.
Monitoring: create alert on (prefetch_cost_tokens > budget_threshold && tail_latency_99 not improving) to auto-disable prefetch globally for the route.

Failure modes: predictor misfires -> wasted prefetch cost (mitigate via conservative priors and max prefetch depth of 3). Chunk mismatch on model switch -> serve stale-safe by validating content hash and re-reading origin if mismatch.
Data pipeline: log training examples for predictor into analytics pipeline (sample 10% of requests) and store in tenant-scoped privacy buckets; ensure PII filtering.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy query-shaping service behind feature flag for console routes: /v1/dashboard/query and /v1/dashboard/explore.
Show tail latency reduction: 99th percentile latency down by >=25% for top 20 tenants with deep-scroll patterns compared to baseline.
Prefetch budget control: prefetch_cost_tokens per-tenant must be capped to configured monthly budget; system should auto-disable prefetch once tenant budget hit with safe fallback response.
No regression in mean latency or error rates; automated integration tests validate cursor parity and idempotent paging across chunk boundaries.
Operational dashboards: prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_cost_tokens, chunk_cache_evictions, and predictor_accuracy available in Console with 14d retention for rollout analysis.

UX consideration: clients may notice slightly different cursor encodings; ensure SDKs decode transparently.
